- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.3) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is weak or negative (e.g., <0.2) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lag in correction: model often delays reacting to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns negative, price correction lags 1–3 days.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and underweights lows — correct by smoothing out extreme recent values.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overconfidence in early periods — reduce forecast magnitude if sentiment is low or volatile.
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model tends to overpredict — apply downward adjustment if sentiment >0.4 and price >65.00.
- If sentiment is low and price is falling, model often underpredicts — adjust upward if sentiment <0.2 and price <60.00.
